peptides.name: Body Protection Compound-157
peptides.description: BPC-157 is a synthetic pentadecapeptide (15 amino acids) derived from a partial sequence of human gastric juice protein BPC. It has been extensively studied in animal models for its effects on wound healing, tissue repair, and cytoprotection of various organ systems. Research has investigated its potential roles in tendon, ligament, muscle, and gastrointestinal healing, as well as neuroprotective effects. It remains a research compound without approved human clinical use.
benefits: Tendon and ligament healing acceleration in animal models
Gastrointestinal cytoprotection and ulcer healing
Muscle injury recovery in preclinical studies
Angiogenesis promotion and blood vessel repair
Neuroprotective effects in animal models of brain injury
Anti-inflammatory activity in various tissue injury models
peptides.mechanism: BPC-157 is thought to exert its effects through modulation of the nitric oxide (NO) system, upregulation of growth factor receptors (including VEGF and EGF receptors), and promotion of angiogenesis. It may also interact with the FAK-paxillin signaling pathway to enhance tendon and tissue repair, and has been shown to modulate dopaminergic and serotonergic systems in the CNS.
contraindications: Pregnancy and breastfeeding (no safety data)
Active malignancies (theoretical concern due to angiogenic properties)
Children (no pediatric safety data)
No human clinical trial safety data available
sideEffects: Limited systematic adverse effect data in humans
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human use by the FDA or other major regulatory agencies. In 2023, the FDA added BPC-157 to its list of substances that cannot be compounded under section 503A/503B of the FD&C Act.

peptides.name: TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4 Fragment)
peptides.description: TB-500 is a synthetic peptide fragment corresponding to the active region (amino acids 17-23, Ac-SDKP region and surrounding sequence) of thymosin beta-4 (Tβ4), a naturally occurring 43-amino acid peptide found in virtually all human and animal cells. Thymosin beta-4 plays a critical role in cell migration, wound healing, and tissue repair through its interaction with actin. Research has investigated TB-500 for its potential effects on wound healing, cardiac repair, reduction of inflammation, and promotion of angiogenesis in various animal models.
benefits: Promotion of wound healing and tissue repair in animal studies
Reduction of inflammation in preclinical models
Promotion of angiogenesis (new blood vessel formation)
Support of cardiac tissue repair following injury in animal models
Enhancement of cell migration and differentiation
Potential improvement of flexibility and reduction of fibrosis
peptides.dosageRange: 2-5 mg per injection, typically 2.0-2.5 mg twice weekly (loading), then 2.0-2.5 mg every 1-2 weeks (maintenance)
peptides.frequency: Twice weekly during loading phase (4-6 weeks), then every 1-2 weeks for maintenance
peptides.mechanism: TB-500 promotes cellular migration by upregulating actin, a protein essential for cell structure and movement, and interacts with actin to promote cell motility and wound healing. It also modulates inflammatory cytokines, promotes angiogenesis, and has been shown to activate cardiac progenitor cells and reduce scar formation in injured tissues.
contraindications: Known or suspected cancer (due to potential promotion of angiogenesis and cell migration)
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Hypersensitivity to thymosin beta-4 or any component
Active malignancies
Not approved for human use — lack of established safety profile
sideEffects: Injection site pain, redness, or swelling
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human use by the FDA. Listed as a prohibited substance by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) under S2 category. Used in veterinary and research contexts. Not approved as a drug or supplement in most jurisdictions.

peptides.name: Thymosin Beta-4
peptides.description: Thymosin Beta-4 (Tβ4) is a naturally occurring 43-amino acid peptide originally isolated from the thymus gland. It is the most abundant member of the beta-thymosin family and is found in nearly all cell types. Research has investigated its roles in wound healing, tissue repair, anti-inflammation, angiogenesis, and cardiac protection. It functions primarily through sequestration of G-actin monomers, regulating actin polymerization and cell motility.
benefits: Wound healing and tissue repair acceleration
Anti-inflammatory effects
Promotion of angiogenesis (new blood vessel formation)
Cardioprotection and cardiac tissue repair after injury
Reduction of fibrosis and scar formation
Promotion of hair growth in preclinical models
peptides.dosageRange: 2-6 mg per administration (research protocols vary widely)
peptides.frequency: 1-2x per week during loading phase, then weekly (varies by protocol)
peptides.mechanism: Thymosin Beta-4 sequesters G-actin monomers to regulate actin-cytoskeleton dynamics, promoting cell migration, survival, and differentiation. It also upregulates anti-inflammatory pathways, promotes angiogenesis via activation of endothelial cell migration, and has been shown to activate the Akt/PI3K survival pathway in cardiomyocytes.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to thymosin beta-4
Active malignancy or history of cancer (theoretical concern due to angiogenic and cell migration properties)
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (insufficient safety data)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved by the FDA for human therapeutic use. RegeneRx Biopharmaceuticals has conducted clinical trials for ophthalmic and dermal wound healing applications. Not approved as a finished drug product.

peptides.name: Long Arginine 3 Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 (IGF-1 LR3)
peptides.description: IGF-1 LR3 is a synthetic, modified analog of human insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1). It contains 83 amino acids, compared to the 70 in native IGF-1, with an arginine substitution at position 3 and a 13-amino-acid N-terminal extension peptide. This modification significantly reduces binding to IGF-binding proteins (IGFBPs), resulting in a longer half-life and greater biological potency. Research has investigated its effects on cell proliferation, muscle hypertrophy, and tissue growth in various in vitro and animal models.
benefits: Enhanced muscle protein synthesis and hypertrophy in research models
Increased cell proliferation and tissue growth
Extended biological activity compared to native IGF-1 due to reduced IGFBP binding
Investigated for anti-catabolic effects on muscle tissue
Studied for potential enhancement of nitrogen retention
Explored in cell culture as a growth factor substitute for serum-free media
peptides.dosageRange: 20-100 mcg/day (research literature references)
peptides.frequency: Once daily, often cited in protocols of 4 weeks on / 2-4 weeks off
peptides.mechanism: IGF-1 LR3 binds to the IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R) and activates downstream PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signaling pathways, promoting cell proliferation, protein synthesis, and inhibition of apoptosis. Its reduced affinity for IGF-binding proteins means a greater fraction remains bioavailable in circulation, enhancing and prolonging its growth-promoting effects compared to endogenous IGF-1.
contraindications: Known or suspected malignancy or active cancer
History of diabetic retinopathy or other proliferative conditions
Hypersensitivity to IGF-1 or any component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Hypoglycemia-prone individuals or those on insulin therapy
Children with closed epiphyses (in a research context)
sideEffects: Jaw pain or facial changes with prolonged use
Organ enlargement (intestinal, cardiac) reported in animal studies
Potential increased risk of tumor growth in susceptible individuals
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human therapeutic use. Mecasermin (recombinant native IGF-1) is FDA-approved for specific conditions, but the LR3 variant is not approved by any regulatory agency for clinical use. Classified as a prohibited substance by WADA.

peptides.name: Des(1-3) Insulin-like Growth Factor 1
peptides.description: IGF-1 DES (Des(1-3) IGF-1) is a truncated variant of insulin-like growth factor 1, lacking the first three amino acids (Gly-Pro-Glu) from the N-terminus. This modification results in significantly reduced binding to IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), making it approximately 10 times more potent than full-length IGF-1 in stimulating cell proliferation and protein synthesis. It has been studied in the context of muscle hypertrophy, cell culture applications, and wound healing research.
benefits: Enhanced muscle protein synthesis compared to intact IGF-1
Increased cell proliferation in research models
Investigated for localized muscle hypertrophy effects
Reduced IGFBP binding allowing greater bioavailability
Studied for potential wound healing acceleration
peptides.dosageRange: 50-150 mcg per administration
peptides.frequency: 1-3x daily, often pre- or post-workout in research protocols
peptides.mechanism: Des(1-3) IGF-1 binds to the IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R) with similar affinity as full-length IGF-1, activating the PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signaling pathways to promote cell survival, proliferation, and protein synthesis. Its truncated N-terminus drastically reduces affinity for IGF binding proteins, resulting in a much higher fraction of free, biologically active peptide compared to intact IGF-1.
contraindications: Active or history of cancer due to potent mitogenic activity
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Hypoglycemia or insulin sensitivity disorders
Pre-existing organ hypertrophy conditions
Individuals under 18 years of age
sideEffects: Localized pain or swelling at injection site
Potential for uncontrolled tissue or organ growth

peptides.name: CJC-1295 with Drug Affinity Complex (DAC)
peptides.description: CJC-1295 with DAC is a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) consisting of 30 amino acids, conjugated with a Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) that binds to serum albumin, dramatically extending its half-life. It was developed by ConjuChem Biotechnologies as a long-acting GHRH analog. Research has investigated its effects on sustained growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) elevation, body composition, and potential therapeutic applications in growth hormone deficiency.
benefits: Sustained elevation of growth hormone levels
Increased IGF-1 concentrations
Investigated for improvements in body composition
Studied for potential effects on lean body mass
Research into enhanced recovery and tissue repair
peptides.dosageRange: 1000-2000 mcg (1-2 mg) per administration
peptides.mechanism: CJC-1295 DAC acts as a GHRH analog that binds to GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotroph cells, stimulating the release of growth hormone in a pulsatile fashion. The DAC moiety covalently binds to circulating albumin via reactive chemistry, preventing rapid renal clearance and extending the peptide's half-life from minutes to approximately 6-8 days, allowing sustained GH and IGF-1 elevation.
contraindications: Active malignancy or history of cancer
Pregnancy and breastfeeding
Pituitary disorders or tumors
Known hypersensitivity to GHRH analogs
Diabetic retinopathy
Children with closed epiphyses
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human use by the FDA or other major regulatory agencies. It was investigated in clinical trials by ConjuChem Biotechnologies but did not achieve regulatory approval.

peptides.name: Modified Growth Hormone Releasing Factor (1-29) / Tetrasubstituted GRF(1-29)
peptides.description: Mod GRF 1-29 (also referred to as CJC-1295 without DAC) is a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) consisting of the first 29 amino acids with four amino acid substitutions (Ala2, Gln8, Ala15, Leu27) to improve metabolic stability and resistance to enzymatic degradation. It acts on the pituitary gland to stimulate the release of growth hormone (GH) in a pulsatile manner. Research has investigated its effects on GH secretion, body composition, and recovery. Unlike the DAC-conjugated version (CJC-1295 with DAC), this form has a shorter duration of action, more closely mimicking natural GH release patterns.

peptides.mechanism: Mod GRF 1-29 binds to GHRH receptors on somatotroph cells of the anterior pituitary gland, activating the cAMP/PKA signaling pathway to stimulate the synthesis and pulsatile release of growth hormone. The four amino acid substitutions confer resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) cleavage and other proteolytic degradation, extending its biological half-life compared to native GHRH(1-29).

peptides.name: Ipamorelin
peptides.description: Ipamorelin is a synthetic pentapeptide growth hormone secretagogue that selectively stimulates growth hormone release from the pituitary gland by acting as a ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R) agonist. Developed by Novo Nordisk in the 1990s, it is distinguished from other GH secretagogues by its selectivity — it does not significantly affect cortisol, prolactin, or ACTH levels at GH-releasing doses. Research has investigated its effects on growth hormone release, bone health, body composition, and gastrointestinal function.
benefits: Selective stimulation of growth hormone release
Investigated for improvement of bone mineral density
Studied for effects on body composition and lean mass
Researched for post-operative gastrointestinal recovery
Minimal impact on cortisol and prolactin compared to other GH secretagogues
peptides.dosageRange: 200-300 mcg per administration
peptides.mechanism: Ipamorelin acts as a selective agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) on pituitary somatotroph cells, stimulating the release of growth hormone in a dose-dependent manner. Unlike GHRP-6 and other GH secretagogues, it does not significantly stimulate the release of ACTH, cortisol, or prolactin at physiological GH-releasing doses, making it one of the most selective GH secretagogues identified.
contraindications: Active malignancy or history of cancer
Pregnancy and breastfeeding
Hypersensitivity to ipamorelin or excipients
Pituitary tumors or disorders
Children with open epiphyseal growth plates (unless under medical supervision)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved by the FDA for human therapeutic use. It has been investigated in clinical trials but has not received regulatory approval for any indication.

peptides.name: Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-2
peptides.description: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin) is a synthetic hexapeptide that acts as a growth hormone secretagogue by binding to the ghrelin/GHS-R1a receptor. It was one of the first synthetic growth hormone releasing peptides developed and has been extensively studied for its potent stimulation of growth hormone release from the anterior pituitary. Research has investigated its effects on GH secretion, appetite regulation, and potential diagnostic use for growth hormone deficiency. In Japan, it has been approved as a diagnostic agent for assessing GH secretion (marketed as GHRP Kaken).

Stimulation of appetite via ghrelin receptor activation
Investigated for diagnostic assessment of GH deficiency
Investigated for potential increase in lean body mass
Studied for effects on sleep quality improvement

peptides.dosageRange: 100-300 mcg per administration
peptides.mechanism: GHRP-2 acts as an agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a), the endogenous receptor for ghrelin, stimulating the release of growth hormone from somatotroph cells in the anterior pituitary. It also suppresses somatostatin activity and may amplify the natural pulsatile release of GH through hypothalamic signaling pathways.

peptides.regulatoryStatus: Approved in Japan as a diagnostic agent for GH deficiency (as pralmorelin/GHRP Kaken). Not FDA-approved in the United States. Classified as a research chemical in most other countries. Listed as a prohibited substance by WADA.

peptides.name: Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-6
peptides.description: GHRP-6 is a synthetic hexapeptide that acts as a potent growth hormone secretagogue by binding to the ghrelin/GHS-R1a receptor in the hypothalamus and pituitary gland. It was one of the first growth hormone releasing peptides discovered, consisting of the sequence His-D-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2. Research has investigated its effects on growth hormone release, appetite stimulation, cardioprotection, and wound healing. It is widely used as a research tool to study the GH axis and ghrelin receptor signaling.

peptides.description: Hexarelin is a synthetic hexapeptide growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP) composed of six amino acids (His-D-2-methyl-Trp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH₂). Research has investigated its effects on growth hormone release, cardiac function, and neuroprotection. It is considered one of the most potent synthetic GHRPs studied in clinical research.

peptides.name: Sermorelin (Growth Hormone-Releasing Factor 1-29 NH2)
peptides.description: Sermorelin is a synthetic peptide analog consisting of the first 29 amino acids of naturally occurring growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH 1-44). It was developed as a diagnostic and therapeutic agent that stimulates the pituitary gland to produce and secrete endogenous growth hormone. Research has investigated its use in growth hormone deficiency in children and adults, as well as age-related decline in growth hormone secretion. It was previously FDA-approved under the brand name Geref but was discontinued from the market.

peptides.name: Ibutamoren (MK-677)
peptides.description: MK-677 (Ibutamoren) is a non-peptide, orally active growth hormone secretagogue that mimics the action of ghrelin by binding to the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a). It stimulates the release of growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) without significantly affecting cortisol levels. Research has investigated its effects on body composition, bone density, sleep quality, and nitrogen balance in various populations including elderly subjects and GH-deficient individuals.

peptides.mechanism: MK-677 acts as a ghrelin mimetic, binding to the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a) in the hypothalamus and pituitary gland to stimulate pulsatile release of growth hormone. It increases GH secretion by both mimicking ghrelin signaling and suppressing somatostatin tone, leading to sustained elevations in GH and IGF-1 without disrupting the normal pulsatile pattern of GH release.

peptides.description: ARA-290 (cibinetide) is a synthetic 11-amino-acid peptide derived from the structure of erythropoietin (EPO). It selectively activates the innate repair receptor (IRR), a heterodimer of the EPO receptor and the beta common receptor (βcR), without stimulating erythropoiesis. Research has investigated its potential in neuropathic pain, sarcoidosis, diabetic neuropathy, and tissue repair. It represents a non-erythropoietic EPO-derived peptide designed to retain the cytoprotective and anti-inflammatory properties of EPO.
benefits: Reduction of neuropathic pain investigated in clinical trials
Anti-inflammatory effects via innate repair receptor activation
Neuroprotective properties studied in preclinical models
Improvement of small nerve fiber density in diabetic neuropathy research
Tissue repair and cytoprotection studied in ischemia-reperfusion models
Potential metabolic improvements in type 2 diabetes investigated
peptides.dosageRange: 2-8 mg per dose (most clinical trials used 4 mg)
peptides.frequency: Once daily or three times weekly (varied by trial protocol)
peptides.mechanism: ARA-290 selectively binds and activates the innate repair receptor (IRR), a heterocomplex of the erythropoietin receptor (EPOR) and the beta common receptor (CD131/βcR). This activation triggers anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and tissue-protective signaling pathways including JAK2/STAT5 and NF-κB modulation, without stimulating red blood cell production.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cibinetide or its components
Concurrent use of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (theoretical interaction)
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (insufficient safety data)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Investigational drug. Not FDA-approved. Has undergone Phase 2 clinical trials for sarcoidosis and diabetic neuropathy. Designated orphan drug status by the EMA for sarcoidosis.

peptides.name: Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide
peptides.description: Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide (DSIP) is a naturally occurring neuropeptide with the amino acid sequence Trp-Ala-Gly-Gly-Asp-Ala-Ser-Gly-Glu, first isolated from rabbit brain in 1977. It was originally identified for its ability to induce delta (slow-wave) sleep in rabbits when infused into the cerebral ventricles. Research has investigated its roles in sleep modulation, stress response, neuroendocrine regulation, and potential analgesic and anticonvulsant properties. DSIP has been studied in both animal models and limited human trials, though it remains an experimental compound.
benefits: Promotion of delta (slow-wave) sleep patterns in research models
Modulation of stress and cortisol responses
Potential analgesic and pain-modulating effects
Investigated for normalization of disturbed sleep architecture
Studied for possible anticonvulsant and neuroprotective properties
Research into regulation of circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine function
peptides.dosageRange: 25-100 mcg/kg body weight
peptides.frequency: Once daily, typically administered in the evening before sleep
peptides.mechanism: DSIP is believed to act on GABAergic and glutamatergic neurotransmitter systems, modulating sleep-wake cycles by promoting slow-wave (delta) sleep EEG activity. It also appears to influence the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, affecting ACTH and cortisol secretion, and may interact with opioid receptor systems to produce analgesic effects.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to DSIP or related peptides
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (insufficient safety data)
Individuals on CNS depressants or sedative medications
Severe hepatic or renal impairment
Not approved for clinical use — safety profile not fully established
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human therapeutic use by the FDA or EMA. Available as a research peptide in some jurisdictions.

peptides.name: Larazotide acetate
peptides.description: Larazotide acetate (formerly AT-1001) is a synthetic octapeptide derived from Vibrio cholerae zonula occludens toxin (Zot). It acts as a tight junction regulator and has been investigated primarily in clinical trials for celiac disease, where it is studied for its ability to reduce intestinal permeability. It is one of the most advanced non-dietary therapeutic candidates for celiac disease, having progressed through Phase 2 and Phase 3 clinical trials.
benefits: Reduction of intestinal permeability in celiac disease research
Reduction of gluten-induced gastrointestinal symptoms in clinical trials
Tight junction integrity maintenance studied in vitro and in vivo
Potential reduction of zonulin-mediated paracellular transport
Investigated for reduction of celiac disease symptom flares during gluten exposure
peptides.dosageRange: 0.5 mg - 1 mg three times daily (based on Phase 2 clinical trials)
peptides.halfLife: Unknown (acts locally in the gut lumen with minimal systemic absorption)
peptides.mechanism: Larazotide acetate acts locally in the intestinal lumen as a tight junction regulator. It is believed to prevent the opening of intestinal tight junctions triggered by gliadin peptides and zonulin, thereby reducing paracellular permeability and preventing the translocation of immunogenic gluten fragments across the intestinal epithelium.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to larazotide or its components
Not approved for any indication — investigational compound
Safety in pregnancy and lactation has not been established
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Investigational drug. Received FDA Fast Track designation for celiac disease. Not yet approved for human therapeutic use. Phase 3 clinical trials have been conducted.

peptides.name: Liraglutide
peptides.description: Liraglutide is a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that shares 97% sequence homology with native human GLP-1. It is an acylated analog of GLP-1(7-37) with a C-16 fatty acid (palmitic acid) attached via a glutamic acid spacer, which enables binding to albumin and extends its half-life. It is FDA-approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes (as Victoza) and for chronic weight management (as Saxenda). Research has also investigated its potential cardiovascular benefits and neuroprotective properties.
benefits: Improved glycemic control and reduced HbA1c in type 2 diabetes
Significant body weight reduction via appetite suppression
Reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk patients
Improved beta-cell function and insulin secretion
Reduction in systolic blood pressure
Potential neuroprotective effects investigated in neurodegenerative disease models
peptides.dosageRange: 0.6-3.0 mg/day (0.6-1.8 mg for diabetes; up to 3.0 mg for weight management)
peptides.mechanism: Liraglutide acts as a GLP-1 receptor agonist, stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells, suppressing glucagon secretion, slowing gastric emptying, and reducing appetite through central nervous system signaling in hypothalamic areas that regulate hunger and satiety. Its fatty acid modification allows reversible albumin binding, protecting it from DPP-4 degradation and extending its duration of action.
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2)
Known hypersensitivity to liraglutide or any excipients
History of pancreatitis (use with caution)
Pregnancy and breastfeeding
Severe gastrointestinal disease including gastroparesis
sideEffects: Hypoglycemia (especially when used with sulfonylureas or insulin)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: FDA-approved: Victoza (1.2-1.8 mg) for type 2 diabetes mellitus (2010), Saxenda (3.0 mg) for chronic weight management (2014). Also EMA-approved.

peptides.name: Thymulin (Facteur Thymique Sérique / Serum Thymic Factor)
peptides.description: Thymulin (also known as Facteur Thymique Sérique or FTS) is a nonapeptide hormone produced by thymic epithelial cells. It requires zinc for biological activity and plays a critical role in T-cell differentiation and maturation. Research has investigated its immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties, as well as its decline with aging and its potential role in immune reconstitution.

Immunomodulatory effects on both innate and adaptive immunity
Anti-inflammatory properties investigated in lung inflammation models
Potential neuroprotective and analgesic effects
Investigated for immune function restoration in aging
Zinc-dependent modulation of immune homeostasis
peptides.dosageRange: Unknown (experimental doses vary widely across animal and in vitro studies)
peptides.halfLife: Unknown (short-lived in circulation; minutes to hours estimated)
peptides.mechanism: Thymulin binds to specific receptors on T-cell precursors and mature T-cells, promoting their differentiation, maturation, and functional activation. In its zinc-bound active form, it modulates cytokine production, influences hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis signaling, and exerts anti-inflammatory effects through inhibition of pro-inflammatory mediators.

Hypersensitivity to thymic peptides
Pregnancy and lactation (insufficient safety data)
sideEffects: Potential immune dysregulation at high doses

peptides.name: Dipeptide Diaminobutyroyl Benzylamide Diacetate (Syn-Ake)
peptides.description: Syn-Ake is a synthetic tripeptide that mimics the activity of waglerin-1, a peptide found in the venom of the Temple Viper (Tropidechis wagleri). It was developed by the Swiss company Pentapharm as a cosmetic active ingredient designed to reduce the appearance of wrinkles. Research has investigated its ability to act as a reversible antagonist of the muscular nicotinic acetylcholine receptor, potentially reducing muscle contractions that contribute to expression lines.

Smoothing of skin surface texture
Reversible inhibition of muscle contraction at the neuromuscular junction
Potential alternative to botulinum toxin-based cosmetic treatments
Improvement in overall skin appearance with topical application
peptides.dosageRange: Typically used at 1-4% concentration in topical cosmetic formulations
peptides.mechanism: Syn-Ake acts as a competitive reversible antagonist of the muscular nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR), similar to the mechanism of waglerin-1. By blocking acetylcholine binding at the neuromuscular junction, it reduces the frequency and intensity of muscle contractions that contribute to dynamic wrinkle formation.
contraindications: Known allergy to any component of the formulation
Individuals with neuromuscular disorders such as myasthenia gravis
Open wounds or broken skin at the application site

sideEffects: Mild skin irritation at application site
Redness or erythema in sensitive individuals

peptides.name: Palmitoyl Pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl)
peptides.description: Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, also known as Pal-KTTKS) is a synthetic lipopeptide consisting of a palmitoyl group attached to the pentapeptide Lys-Thr-Thr-Lys-Ser. It is derived from a fragment of procollagen I C-terminal propeptide and is widely used as a cosmetic active ingredient. Research has investigated its ability to stimulate collagen synthesis, fibronectin production, and extracellular matrix remodeling in dermal fibroblasts, positioning it as a key ingredient in anti-wrinkle skincare formulations.
benefits: Stimulation of collagen I and III synthesis in fibroblasts
Promotion of fibronectin production
Reduction in appearance of fine lines and wrinkles in clinical studies
Stimulation of extracellular matrix component production
Improvement of skin texture and firmness
peptides.dosageRange: Typically used at 2-8% concentration in topical formulations (as Matrixyl solution containing ~100 ppm active pentapeptide)
peptides.mechanism: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 acts as a matrikine — a messenger peptide fragment derived from extracellular matrix proteins that signals fibroblasts to increase production of collagen, fibronectin, and other matrix components. The palmitoyl chain enhances skin penetration and cellular uptake, while the KTTKS sequence, derived from the C-terminal propeptide of type I procollagen, activates fibroblast signaling pathways involved in extracellular matrix remodeling.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to any component of the formulation
Broken or severely compromised skin barrier
Active skin infections at the application site
sideEffects: Mild skin irritation in sensitive individuals
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Cosmetic ingredient approved for use in skincare products. Not classified as a drug. Listed in the International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients (INCI). Not FDA-approved as a pharmaceutical.

peptides.name: Semax (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro)
peptides.description: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide derived from the N-terminal fragment of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH 4-10) with an added C-terminal tripeptide Pro-Gly-Pro. It was developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences. Semax is approved in Russia as a nootropic and neuroprotective agent, and research has investigated its effects on cognitive function, neurogenesis, and neuroprotection following ischemic brain injury.
benefits: Neuroprotective effects studied in cerebral ischemia models
Cognitive enhancement and memory improvement investigated in research
Modulation of BDNF and NGF expression studied in animal models
Anxiolytic and antidepressant-like effects explored in preclinical research
Potential improvement in attention and learning investigated
Anti-inflammatory effects in the central nervous system studied
peptides.dosageRange: 50-600 mcg per administration (intranasal); up to 1200 mcg/day in some Russian clinical studies
peptides.halfLife: ~30 seconds to several minutes (parent peptide); prolonged pharmacological effects due to active metabolites
peptides.mechanism: Semax modulates the expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and nerve growth factor (NGF) in the brain, activating neurotrophic signaling cascades via TrkB receptors. It also affects the melanocortin system, modulates dopaminergic and serotonergic neurotransmission, and influences gene expression related to immune response and vascular function in the central nervous system.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to Semax or its components
Acute psychotic disorders
Conditions associated with anxiety (may require caution)
Pregnancy and lactation (insufficient safety data)
sideEffects: Nasal irritation or discomfort at application site
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Approved in Russia and Ukraine as a prescription nootropic drug. Not approved by the FDA for any indication. Classified as a research chemical in most Western countries.

peptides.description: N-Acetyl Semax is a modified analog of Semax, itself a synthetic derivative of the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) fragment 4-10. The N-acetyl modification is designed to improve metabolic stability and bioavailability compared to the parent peptide Semax. Research has investigated its potential neuroprotective, nootropic, and neurotrophic properties, primarily in Russian and Eastern European studies. It has been explored for cognitive enhancement, neurological recovery, and modulation of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression.

Enhancement of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression studied

peptides.name: Selank (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro)
peptides.description: Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide derived from the naturally occurring tetrapeptide tuftsin (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg) with an added Pro-Gly-Pro sequence that confers metabolic stability. Developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences, it is approved in Russia as a nasal spray for anxiety and nootropic purposes. Research has investigated its anxiolytic, nootropic, immunomodulatory, and neuroprotective properties.

Nootropic and memory-enhancing properties studied in animal models
Immunomodulatory effects via influence on cytokine expression
Neuroprotective activity investigated in oxidative stress models
Modulation of gene expression related to GABA and serotonin neurotransmission

peptides.name: Cerebrolysin
peptides.description: Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide preparation consisting of low-molecular-weight neuropeptides and free amino acids obtained by standardized enzymatic breakdown of lipid-free porcine brain proteins. It has been investigated in clinical research for its potential neurotrophic and neuroprotective properties, particularly in the context of stroke, traumatic brain injury, Alzheimer's disease, and vascular dementia. It is approved as a prescription medication in several countries but is not FDA-approved in the United States.

Studied for potential cognitive improvement in Alzheimer's disease
Researched for neurotrophic factor-like activity supporting neuronal survival
Investigated for recovery enhancement after traumatic brain injury

peptides.mechanism: Cerebrolysin mimics the action of endogenous neurotrophic factors, promoting neuronal sprouting, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis while reducing amyloid-beta deposition and tau hyperphosphorylation. Epilepsy or status epilepticus
Severe renal impairment
Pregnancy and lactation (insufficient safety data)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Approved as a prescription drug in over 40 countries (including in Europe and Asia) for neurological conditions. Not FDA-approved in the United States.

It corresponds to the FG loop region of NCAM that interacts with the fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1). Research has investigated FGL for its neurotrophic and neuroprotective properties, including effects on synaptic plasticity, memory formation, and neuroinflammation in preclinical models of neurodegeneration and brain injury.

peptides.mechanism: FGL acts as an agonist of fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1), mimicking the binding interaction of the NCAM FG loop to activate FGFR1 signaling cascades including the MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt pathways. peptides.name: N-hexanoyl-Tyr-Ile-(6)-aminohexanoic amide (Dihexa)
peptides.description: Dihexa is a synthetic hexapeptide analog derived from angiotensin IV. Research has investigated its potential as a cognitive enhancer, with animal studies suggesting it may be orders of magnitude more potent than brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) in promoting new synapse formation. It remains an experimental research compound not approved for human use.

Improvement of cognitive function in scopolamine-impaired animal models
Augmentation of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF)/c-Met signaling
Promotion of dendritic spine formation in preclinical research

peptides.dosageRange: Unknown (animal studies used doses in the range of 0.1-2 mg/kg; no established human dosages exist)
peptides.mechanism: Dihexa acts as an allosteric modulator of the hepatocyte growth factor (HGF)/c-Met receptor system, stabilizing HGF and potentiating its binding to the c-Met receptor. This activation promotes pro-neurotrophic signaling pathways involved in synaptogenesis, dendritic spine formation, and neuronal connectivity.

Potential concern for individuals with cancer history due to HGF/c-Met pathway involvement in tumor growth
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (unknown safety)
Individuals with known hypersensitivity to any component
sideEffects: Theoretical concern for pro-tumorigenic effects via c-Met activation
Blood pressure changes (theoretical, due to angiotensin system relationship)

It was designed as a neurotrophic compound that can penetrate the blood-brain barrier when administered orally. Research has investigated its potential role in enhancing neurogenesis, reducing tau pathology, and preventing neurodegeneration in animal models of Alzheimer's disease and related disorders.

peptides.name: PE-22-28 (Spadin analog / Sortilin-derived peptide fragment)
peptides.description: PE-22-28 is a synthetic heptapeptide derived from the propeptide of sortilin (residues 22-28 of the pro-domain). It acts as an antagonist of the TREK-1 potassium channel, a mechanism linked to antidepressant-like effects. Research has investigated its potential as a rapid-acting antidepressant compound in animal models, building on work with the parent peptide spadin. PE-22-28 demonstrates improved stability and potency compared to spadin.

Research has investigated its effects on memory, learning, neuroprotection, and cognitive enhancement in both animal models and human clinical trials. It is approved as a prescription nootropic in Russia but remains unapproved for clinical use in most other countries.

peptides.name: Afamelanotide (Melanotan I)
peptides.description: Melanotan I (afamelanotide) is a synthetic linear analog of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) consisting of 13 amino acids. It was developed at the University of Arizona and acts as a non-selective melanocortin receptor agonist. Research has primarily investigated its ability to stimulate melanogenesis (skin pigmentation) and its potential photoprotective properties, particularly in patients with photosensitivity disorders such as erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP).

peptides.mechanism: Afamelanotide binds to melanocortin 1 receptors (MC1R) on melanocytes, activating adenylate cyclase and increasing intracellular cAMP levels. This stimulates the production of eumelanin, the dark photoprotective pigment, independent of UV exposure, thereby enhancing the skin's natural defense against ultraviolet radiation damage.

Severe hepatic impairment
Severe renal impairment

Pregnancy and lactation

peptides.name: Bremelanotide (PT-141)

Research has primarily focused on its effects on sexual dysfunction, and it received FDA approval in 2019 for the treatment of hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women.

peptides.name: Humanin
peptides.description: Humanin is a 24-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide (MDP) encoded within the 16S ribosomal RNA gene of mitochondrial DNA. It was first identified in 2001 from a cDNA library of surviving neurons in Alzheimer's disease brains. Research has investigated its roles in cytoprotection, neuroprotection, metabolic regulation, and aging. Humanin and its analogs (such as HNG, a potent S14G variant) have been studied extensively in preclinical models of neurodegeneration, cardiovascular disease, and age-related decline.

peptides.mechanism: Humanin exerts cytoprotective effects through binding to the trimeric receptor complex composed of CNTFR, WSX-1, and gp130 (IL-27 receptor), activating STAT3 signaling pathways. It also interacts intracellularly with BAX to inhibit mitochondrial apoptosis, binds IGFBP-3 to modulate IGF signaling, and activates AMPK pathways to improve metabolic function.

peptides.description: MOTS-c is a 16-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide (MDP) encoded within the 12S rRNA gene of mitochondrial DNA. It was first identified in 2015 by Changhan Lee and colleagues at the University of Southern California. Research has investigated its role in metabolic regulation, particularly in glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, and exercise-mimicking effects. MOTS-c is notable as a mitochondrial-encoded signaling peptide that translocates to the nucleus under metabolic stress to regulate gene expression.

peptides.name: Elamipretide (SS-31, Bendavia, MTP-131)
peptides.description: Elamipretide (SS-31) is a synthetic mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide with the sequence D-Arg-dimethylTyr-Lys-Phe-NH2. Research has investigated its potential in mitochondrial myopathies, heart failure, age-related macular degeneration, and other conditions associated with mitochondrial dysfunction. It has been evaluated in multiple clinical trials but has not yet received FDA approval.

peptides.mechanism: SS-31 selectively targets and binds to cardiolipin on the inner mitochondrial membrane, stabilizing cristae architecture and optimizing electron transport chain supercomplex organization. This interaction reduces electron leak and excessive ROS generation, restores mitochondrial membrane potential, and enhances oxidative phosphorylation efficiency.

It is a D-retro-inverso (DRI) version of the FOXO4-p53 interfering peptide, meaning it uses D-amino acids in a reversed sequence to increase proteolytic stability while maintaining binding activity. Research has investigated its potential as a senolytic agent to clear damaged, aging cells and restore tissue homeostasis in preclinical models.

By freeing p53 from FOXO4 sequestration, p53 is redirected to the mitochondria where it triggers the intrinsic apoptotic pathway, selectively killing senescent cells while sparing healthy, non-senescent cells.

peptides.name: Khavinson Peptide Bioregulators
peptides.description: Khavinson peptide bioregulators are a class of short peptides (typically 2-4 amino acids) developed by Professor Vladimir Khavinson at the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology. Originally isolated from animal organ extracts, these peptides are proposed to interact with specific DNA sequences and regulate gene expression in corresponding tissues. Research has investigated their potential roles in aging, organ-specific function restoration, and geroprotection. Notable examples include Epithalon (AGAG), Vilon (KE), Thymogen (EW), Livagen (EKDK), and Pinealon (EDR).

This epigenetic regulation mechanism is proposed to restore declining protein synthesis associated with aging, effectively acting as short signaling molecules that normalize gene expression patterns.

peptides.name: Thymosin Alpha-1
peptides.description: Thymosin alpha-1 is a 28-amino acid peptide originally isolated from thymic tissue (thymosin fraction 5) by Allan Goldstein and colleagues in the 1970s. It plays a central role in immune system modulation, particularly in the maturation and differentiation of T cells. Research has investigated its potential in chronic viral infections (hepatitis B and C), immunodeficiency states, cancer immunotherapy, and as a vaccine adjuvant. A synthetic version (thymalfasin) is approved in several countries outside the United States for the treatment of hepatitis B and as an immune-enhancing agent.
benefits: Enhancement of T-cell maturation and differentiation
Modulation of dendritic cell and natural killer cell activity
Investigated as adjunct therapy for chronic hepatitis B and C
Researched as immunotherapy adjuvant in cancer treatment
Investigated for enhancement of vaccine immunogenicity
Studied for potential benefit in sepsis and immunocompromised states
peptides.dosageRange: 1.6 mg (subcutaneous injection)
peptides.frequency: 2x weekly or daily depending on study protocol
peptides.mechanism: Thymosin alpha-1 acts on toll-like receptors (TLR2 and TLR9) on dendritic cells and other immune cells, promoting the maturation, differentiation, and activation of T lymphocytes, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells. It enhances both innate and adaptive immune responses by upregulating cytokine production (including IL-2, IFN-alpha, and IFN-gamma) and increasing MHC class I expression.

Patients on immunosuppressive therapy (potential interaction)
Organ transplant recipients (risk of graft rejection due to immune activation)
sideEffects: Generally well-tolerated in clinical trials with a favorable safety profile
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Approved in over 35 countries (including Italy, China, and several other nations) under the trade name Zadaxin for hepatitis B and as an immune modulator. Not FDA-approved in the United States. Classified as an orphan drug by the FDA for certain indications.

peptides.name: Arginyl-Glycyl-Cysteine (RG-Cys)
peptides.description: RG-Cys (Arg-Gly-Cys) is a tripeptide composed of arginine, glycine, and cysteine residues. It is structurally related to the redox-active tripeptide glutathione (GSH) and has been investigated in research contexts for its potential antioxidant properties and its role as a building block in peptide chemistry. The cysteine residue provides a free thiol group that may participate in redox reactions and metal chelation. Research has explored its interactions in the context of oxidative stress modulation and as a component of larger bioactive sequences.

peptides.name: Transfer Factor
peptides.description: Transfer factor is a mixture of small molecular weight molecules (less than 10 kDa) derived from leukocyte lysates, originally described by H. Sherwood Lawrence in 1955. These dialyzable leukocyte extracts (DLE) are composed of peptides, amino acids, and small RNA fragments that are believed to transfer cell-mediated immunity from an immune donor to a non-immune recipient. Research has investigated their potential role in modulating immune responses in various infectious, neoplastic, and immunodeficiency conditions. Transfer factors are not single defined peptides but rather complex mixtures of immunomodulatory molecules.

Enhancement of delayed-type hypersensitivity reactions

They are thought to interact with T-cell receptors or antigen-presenting cells, upregulating cytokine production (including interferon-gamma and interleukin-2) and enhancing natural killer cell activity.

peptides.name: Semaglutide
peptides.description: Semaglutide is a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist originally developed by Novo Nordisk. It is a modified analog of human GLP-1 with 94% structural homology, featuring key amino acid substitutions and a C-18 fatty diacid chain that enable extended duration of action. It is FDA-approved for the treatment of type 2 diabetes (Ozempic, Rybelsus) and chronic weight management (Wegovy). Research continues to investigate its potential cardiovascular, hepatic, and neuroprotective effects.
benefits: Improved glycemic control and HbA1c reduction in type 2 diabetes
Significant body weight reduction through appetite suppression
Reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events in at-risk populations
Improvement in non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) markers

peptides.mechanism: Semaglutide binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor, stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon release, slowing gastric emptying, and reducing appetite through central nervous system signaling in the hypothalamus. The C-18 fatty diacid side chain enables strong albumin binding, which protects against DPP-4 degradation and extends its plasma half-life to approximately one week.

peptides.regulatoryStatus: FDA-approved: Ozempic (0.5 mg, 1 mg, 2 mg) for type 2 diabetes mellitus (2017); Rybelsus (oral, 3/7/14 mg) for type 2 diabetes (2019); Wegovy (2.4 mg) for chronic weight management (2021). Also approved by the EMA and regulatory agencies in many other countries.

Research has investigated its effects on appetite regulation, body weight reduction, and glycemic control, both as a monotherapy and in combination with semaglutide (a GLP-1 receptor agonist) under the combination program CagriSema.

Research has primarily been conducted in vitro using C2C12 myoblast cell lines, and no human clinical trials have been published.

peptides.description: Adipotide, also known as FTPP (Fat-Targeted Proapoptotic Peptide), is a synthetic chimeric peptide designed to target and destroy blood vessels supplying white adipose tissue. It consists of a prohibitin-targeting sequence (CKGGRAKDC) linked to a proapoptotic peptide D(KLAKLAK)2. Originally developed at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, it was initially investigated as a vascular-targeting agent in cancer research before being studied for its effects on obesity in non-human primate models.

This leads to destruction of blood supply to fat tissue, causing adipocyte death and resorption of white fat deposits.

peptides.name: Palmitoyl Oligopeptide (Biopeptide EL)

peptides.name: Gonadorelin (Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone)

peptides.name: Leuprolide (Leuprorelin)
peptides.description: Leuprolide is a synthetic nonapeptide analog of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH/LHRH) that acts as a potent GnRH receptor agonist. Upon continuous administration, it paradoxically suppresses gonadotropin secretion and subsequently reduces sex hormone production through receptor desensitization and downregulation. It is FDA-approved and widely used in clinical medicine for conditions including prostate cancer, endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and central precocious puberty. Research continues to explore its applications in reproductive medicine, oncology, and hormone-dependent conditions.

This results in profound suppression of LH and FSH secretion, leading to marked reduction in gonadal sex steroid production (testosterone in males, estradiol in females) to castrate or postmenopausal levels.

Magainin 2, the most studied variant, is a 23-amino acid cationic peptide with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against bacteria, fungi, and protozoa. Research has investigated its potential as a novel antibiotic agent and its mechanism of membrane disruption, as well as potential anticancer properties.

peptides.name: Human Defensin (Alpha-Defensin / HNP-1)
peptides.description: Defensins are a family of small (2-6 kDa) cysteine-rich cationic antimicrobial peptides found in humans and other vertebrates. They are key components of the innate immune system, produced primarily by neutrophils and epithelial cells. Human defensins are classified into alpha-defensins (HNP-1 through HNP-4 and HD-5, HD-6) and beta-defensins (hBD-1 through hBD-4). Research has investigated their roles in direct antimicrobial killing, immunomodulation, wound healing, and potential therapeutic applications against infectious diseases and cancer.

peptides.name: Lactoferrin
peptides.description: Lactoferrin is a multifunctional glycoprotein belonging to the transferrin family, naturally found in mammalian milk (particularly colostrum), saliva, tears, and other mucosal secretions. It consists of approximately 690 amino acids and has iron-binding properties. Research has investigated its antimicrobial, antiviral, antifungal, immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and prebiotic activities. It is one of the most studied bioactive proteins in human and bovine milk.

Iron-binding and iron homeostasis support
Immunomodulatory effects on innate and adaptive immunity
Anti-inflammatory properties in gut and systemic tissues

peptides.mechanism: Lactoferrin exerts antimicrobial effects by sequestering iron essential for bacterial growth and by directly binding to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) on gram-negative bacterial membranes, disrupting their integrity. It also modulates immune responses by interacting with immune cell receptors, promoting T-cell maturation, enhancing natural killer cell activity, and regulating cytokine production to balance pro- and anti-inflammatory responses.

peptides.name: Nisin
peptides.description: Nisin is a polycyclic antimicrobial peptide produced by the bacterium Lactococcus lactis. It is composed of 34 amino acid residues and contains several unusual amino acids including lanthionine and dehydroalanine, classifying it as a lantibiotic. Nisin has been widely studied for its potent antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive bacteria and has a long history of use as a food preservative. Research has also investigated its potential anticancer, immunomodulatory, and oral health applications.

Investigated for anticancer properties in preclinical models
Effective food biopreservative with GRAS status
Researched for oral health applications against dental pathogens

peptides.mechanism: Nisin exerts its antimicrobial action through a dual mechanism: it binds to lipid II, a key precursor molecule in bacterial cell wall synthesis, thereby inhibiting cell wall formation. This binding also facilitates the formation of pores in the bacterial cytoplasmic membrane, leading to rapid cell death through loss of membrane integrity and leakage of intracellular contents.

sideEffects: Generally recognized as safe (GRAS) for food use

peptides.name: Polymyxin B
peptides.description: Polymyxin B is a cyclic lipopeptide antibiotic produced by Paenibacillus polymyxa (formerly Bacillus polymyxa). It was discovered in 1947 and is primarily used as a last-resort treatment for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections, particularly those caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Research continues to investigate its pharmacokinetics, optimal dosing strategies, and its well-known ability to bind and neutralize bacterial lipopolysaccharide (endotoxin).

Binding and neutralization of lipopolysaccharide (endotoxin)

peptides.name: Gramicidin
peptides.description: Gramicidin is a heterogeneous mixture of linear antimicrobial peptides produced by the soil bacterium Brevibacillus brevis (formerly Bacillus brevis). It consists primarily of gramicidin A, B, and C, which are 15-amino-acid peptides composed largely of alternating L- and D-amino acids. Research has extensively investigated its ion channel-forming properties and its use as a topical antibiotic agent against Gram-positive bacteria. It is a classic model system for studying membrane ion channels and peptide-lipid interactions.

Ion channel formation in lipid bilayers used as a biophysical research tool

peptides.name: Bacitracin
peptides.description: Bacitracin is a mixture of cyclic polypeptide antibiotics produced by Bacillus subtilis and Bacillus licheniformis. First isolated in 1945, it primarily inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by interfering with the dephosphorylation of C55-isoprenyl pyrophosphate (undecaprenyl pyrophosphate), a lipid carrier essential for peptidoglycan synthesis. It is most effective against Gram-positive bacteria and is widely used as a topical antibiotic for the prevention and treatment of minor skin infections.

peptides.name: Insulin (human recombinant)
peptides.description: Insulin is a 51-amino acid peptide hormone produced by the beta cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans. It is the primary regulator of blood glucose homeostasis, facilitating cellular uptake of glucose from the bloodstream. First isolated in 1921 by Banting and Best, insulin has been used therapeutically since 1922 for the management of diabetes mellitus. Modern insulin preparations are produced via recombinant DNA technology and are available in rapid-acting, short-acting, intermediate-acting, and long-acting formulations.

peptides.name: Glucagon
peptides.description: Glucagon is a 29-amino acid peptide hormone produced by the alpha cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans. It serves as a critical counter-regulatory hormone to insulin, playing a central role in glucose homeostasis by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Glucagon is FDA-approved for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia and is also used as a diagnostic aid in radiologic examinations of the gastrointestinal tract. Research continues to investigate its role in metabolic regulation, obesity, and novel dual/triple agonist therapies targeting glucagon and GLP-1 receptors.

It acts as a potent endogenous mediator of inflammation, vasodilation, and pain signaling. Bradykinin has also been studied in the context of COVID-19 pathology due to its role in the renin-angiotensin system.

Research has investigated its roles in satiety and appetite regulation, gastrointestinal motility, thermoregulation, and its potential involvement in certain cancers where bombesin-like peptide receptors are overexpressed.

peptides.name: Cecropin A

peptides.name: Corticotropin-Releasing Hormone
peptides.description: Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) is a 41-amino acid neuropeptide produced primarily in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus. It is the principal regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, stimulating the release of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) from the anterior pituitary. Research has investigated CRH's roles in stress responses, anxiety, depression, inflammatory conditions, and as a diagnostic tool for Cushing's syndrome and adrenal insufficiency.

peptides.name: Dynorphin A (1-17)
peptides.description: Dynorphin A is a 17-amino acid endogenous opioid peptide derived from the precursor protein prodynorphin. It is the primary endogenous ligand for the kappa-opioid receptor (KOR) and is widely distributed in the central nervous system, including the hypothalamus, hippocampus, striatum, and spinal cord. Research has investigated its roles in pain modulation, stress responses, mood regulation, reward circuitry, and addiction. Dynorphin A is also studied for its involvement in dysphoria, learning, memory, and neuroendocrine signaling.

peptides.name: Melanin-Concentrating Hormone
peptides.description: Melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH) is a cyclic 19-amino acid neuropeptide predominantly produced in the lateral hypothalamus and zona incerta. It acts through two G protein-coupled receptors, MCHR1 (widely expressed in mammals) and MCHR2 (found in primates and some other species). Research has extensively investigated MCH's roles in energy homeostasis, feeding behavior, sleep regulation, and mood. MCH is considered orexigenic (appetite-stimulating), and antagonism of its receptor system has been explored as a potential approach for obesity and metabolic disorders.
benefits: Regulation of energy balance and feeding behavior
Modulation of sleep architecture, particularly REM sleep
Involvement in glucose metabolism and insulin sensitivity
Roles in mood and stress response regulation
Pigmentation regulation in fish (original discovery context)
peptides.dosageRange: Unknown
peptides.mechanism: MCH binds to MCHR1 (and MCHR2 in primates), both Gi/Go-coupled receptors, leading to inhibition of adenylyl cyclase and activation of downstream signaling cascades including ERK and Akt pathways. In the hypothalamus, MCH signaling promotes food intake, reduces energy expenditure, and modulates reward circuits, while in other brain regions it influences REM sleep and emotional processing.
contraindications: Not approved for human therapeutic use
Potential interactions with metabolic or mood-related conditions
Pregnancy and lactation (insufficient data)
Individuals with eating disorders
sideEffects: Increased appetite and food intake (observed in animal models)
Potential anxiogenic or depressive-like effects at certain doses
Weight gain with chronic exposure (animal models)
commonStacks: Orexin/Hypocretin (researched in parallel for sleep-wake regulation)
Neuropeptide Y (co-investigated in feeding behavior studies)
Alpha-MSH (functionally antagonistic peptide in energy balance)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human therapeutic use. MCH receptor antagonists have been investigated in clinical trials for obesity but none are currently FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Melanocortin Peptides (α-MSH / Melanocortin System)
peptides.description: Melanocortins are a family of peptide hormones derived from the precursor protein proopiomelanocortin (POMC), including α-MSH, β-MSH, γ-MSH, and ACTH. They act through five melanocortin receptor subtypes (MC1R–MC5R) and play critical roles in pigmentation, energy homeostasis, appetite regulation, inflammation, and sexual function. Research has investigated melanocortin analogs such as melanotan II and setmelanotide for their effects on obesity, skin pigmentation, and metabolic regulation. The melanocortin system is one of the most studied neuroendocrine signaling pathways in energy balance and body weight regulation.

Regulation of skin and hair pigmentation via MC1R
Anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects
Modulation of sexual function and arousal
Potential role in cardiovascular regulation
Research into treatment of genetic obesity syndromes

peptides.halfLife: α-MSH: ~20 minutes endogenously; synthetic analogs vary (setmelanotide ~11 hours)
peptides.mechanism: Melanocortin peptides bind to melanocortin receptors (MC1R–MC5R), which are G-protein coupled receptors that activate adenylyl cyclase and increase intracellular cAMP. MC4R activation in the hypothalamus suppresses appetite and increases energy expenditure, while MC1R activation in melanocytes stimulates eumelanin production and modulates inflammatory signaling in immune cells.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to melanocortin peptides
History of melanoma or predisposition to melanocytic neoplasms
Pregnancy and breastfeeding
Significant hepatic or renal impairment
Cardiovascular disease (due to potential effects on blood pressure)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Setmelanotide (Imcivree) is FDA-approved for obesity due to POMC, PCSK1, or LEPR deficiency. Most other melanocortin analogs (e.g., melanotan I, melanotan II) are not approved for human therapeutic use and are classified as research chemicals. Bremelanotide (PT-141/Vyleesi) is FDA-approved for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women.

peptides.name: Motilin
peptides.description: Motilin is a 22-amino acid endogenous peptide hormone primarily secreted by enterochromaffin cells (Mo cells) of the upper small intestine. It plays a key role in regulating gastrointestinal motility, specifically initiating the migrating motor complex (MMC) during fasting. Research has investigated motilin's role in gastric emptying, appetite regulation, and gastrointestinal motility disorders. Erythromycin and related macrolide antibiotics act as motilin receptor agonists, which has driven significant pharmacological interest.
benefits: Stimulation of gastrointestinal motility and migrating motor complex
Promotion of gastric emptying
Regulation of interdigestive gut motor activity
Modulation of appetite and hunger signaling
Research into gastroparesis and functional dyspepsia treatment
peptides.dosageRange: Unknown — endogenous hormone; research studies have used IV infusions of 0.4–4.0 pmol/kg/min
peptides.frequency: Unknown — typically administered as continuous IV infusion in research settings
peptides.mechanism: Motilin binds to the motilin receptor (MLNR/GPR38), a G-protein coupled receptor expressed on smooth muscle cells and enteric neurons of the gastrointestinal tract, activating intracellular calcium signaling pathways. This triggers phase III contractions of the migrating motor complex in the stomach and upper small intestine during the interdigestive (fasting) state, facilitating clearance of undigested material.
contraindications: Mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction
Gastrointestinal perforation
Known hypersensitivity to motilin or analogs
Acute gastrointestinal hemorrhage
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research compound; not approved as a therapeutic agent. Endogenous peptide hormone studied in clinical research settings. Motilin receptor agonists (e.g., erythromycin) are used off-label for gastroparesis.

peptides.name: Neuropeptide Y
peptides.description: Neuropeptide Y is a 36-amino acid peptide neurotransmitter widely distributed in the central and peripheral nervous systems. It is one of the most abundant neuropeptides in the brain, particularly concentrated in the hypothalamus. Research has investigated its roles in appetite regulation, energy homeostasis, stress response, anxiety modulation, circadian rhythms, and cardiovascular function. NPY acts through a family of G-protein coupled receptors (Y1-Y5) and is considered a potent orexigenic (appetite-stimulating) factor.
benefits: Appetite and energy homeostasis regulation studied in metabolic research
Stress resilience and anxiolytic effects investigated in preclinical models
Cardiovascular regulation including vasoconstriction and blood pressure modulation
Bone formation and remodeling effects studied in skeletal research
Neuroprotective properties investigated in neurodegeneration models
Role in circadian rhythm and sleep regulation explored
peptides.dosageRange: Unknown — primarily studied via central or peripheral administration in preclinical models; no established human dosing for exogenous use
peptides.mechanism: NPY binds to Y1, Y2, Y4, and Y5 G-protein coupled receptors, inhibiting adenylyl cyclase and reducing intracellular cAMP levels. In the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus, NPY/AgRP neurons stimulate food intake and reduce energy expenditure, while also modulating sympathetic nervous system activity, anxiety-related circuits in the amygdala, and vascular tone via direct action on smooth muscle.
contraindications: Cardiovascular disease — NPY has potent vasoconstrictive effects
Hypertension — may exacerbate elevated blood pressure
Obesity or metabolic syndrome — potent orexigenic effects may worsen condition
Pregnancy and breastfeeding — insufficient safety data
Not approved for exogenous human administration
sideEffects: Coronary artery vasoconstriction at high doses
commonStacks: Peptide YY (PYY — related peptide in appetite regulation)
AgRP (Agouti-related peptide — co-expressed in hypothalamic neurons)
CRF (Corticotropin-releasing factor — studied in stress axis research)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical and endogenous neuropeptide. Not approved by the FDA for therapeutic use. Used extensively as a research tool in neuroscience and metabolic studies.

peptides.name: Neurotensin
peptides.description: Neurotensin is a 13-amino acid neuropeptide (pGlu-Leu-Tyr-Glu-Asn-Lys-Pro-Arg-Arg-Pro-Tyr-Ile-Leu) originally isolated from bovine hypothalamus by Carraway and Leeman in 1973. It is found in the central nervous system and in enteroendocrine N cells of the gastrointestinal tract. Research has investigated its roles in regulation of fat absorption, body temperature (hypothermia), analgesia, blood pressure modulation, and its involvement in dopaminergic neurotransmission. It has also been studied for its potential relevance in obesity, cancer progression, and neuropsychiatric conditions including schizophrenia.
benefits: Modulation of fat absorption and lipid metabolism in the gut
Analgesic effects comparable to opioids in preclinical models
Hypothermic response and thermoregulation
Modulation of dopaminergic signaling relevant to neuropsychiatric research
Blood pressure regulation through vasodilatory effects
Investigated as a biomarker for cardiometabolic risk and obesity
peptides.dosageRange: Unknown
peptides.halfLife: ~2-3 minutes (plasma, due to rapid enzymatic degradation)
peptides.mechanism: Neurotensin exerts its biological effects primarily through three receptors: NTS1 (NTSR1) and NTS2 (NTSR2), which are G-protein coupled receptors, and NTS3 (sortilin). Activation of NTS1, the high-affinity receptor, mediates most of its peripheral and central effects including hypothermia, analgesia, stimulation of intestinal motility, and modulation of dopamine neurotransmission in mesolimbic and mesocortical pathways.
contraindications: Hypotension or conditions worsened by vasodilation
Known hypersensitivity to neurotensin or its analogs
Concurrent use of antipsychotic medications (potential dopaminergic interactions)
Conditions involving impaired thermoregulation
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human therapeutic use. Studied extensively in preclinical and basic science research settings.

peptides.name: Orexin A (Hypocretin-1)
peptides.description: Orexin A (also known as hypocretin-1) is a 33-amino acid neuropeptide produced by neurons in the lateral hypothalamus. It plays a critical role in regulating wakefulness, arousal, appetite, and energy homeostasis. Research has extensively investigated its role in narcolepsy, where orexin-producing neurons are destroyed, as well as its involvement in reward pathways, feeding behavior, and metabolic regulation. Orexin A acts through two G-protein coupled receptors, OX1R and OX2R, widely distributed throughout the brain.
benefits: Promotion of wakefulness and arousal
Regulation of sleep-wake cycles
Modulation of appetite and feeding behavior
Enhancement of cognitive alertness and attention
Regulation of energy metabolism and thermogenesis
Involvement in reward processing and motivation
peptides.dosageRange: Unknown (most human research uses indirect modulation; animal studies use 1-10 nmol intracerebroventricular or 10-100 mcg intranasal)
peptides.mechanism: Orexin A binds to orexin receptor 1 (OX1R) and orexin receptor 2 (OX2R), both G-protein coupled receptors, activating downstream signaling cascades including phospholipase C and calcium mobilization. This promotes neuronal excitability in wake-promoting brain regions including the locus coeruleus, tuberomammillary nucleus, and dorsal raphe, thereby sustaining wakefulness, arousal, and autonomic tone.
contraindications: Insomnia or hyperarousal disorders
Anxiety disorders (may exacerbate symptoms)
Cardiovascular conditions (orexin A can increase sympathetic tone and blood pressure)
Concurrent use of orexin receptor antagonists (e.g., suvorexant)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human therapeutic use. Orexin receptor agonists (e.g., danavorexton/TAK-994) are under clinical investigation for narcolepsy but are not yet approved.

peptides.name: Orexin B (Hypocretin-2)
peptides.description: Orexin B (also known as hypocretin-2) is a 28-amino acid neuropeptide produced by neurons in the lateral hypothalamus. It is derived from the same prepro-orexin precursor as orexin A and acts primarily through the orexin-2 receptor (OX2R). Research has investigated its roles in sleep-wake regulation, arousal, appetite, energy homeostasis, and reward-seeking behavior. Deficiency of orexin signaling is strongly implicated in narcolepsy type 1.
benefits: Promotion of wakefulness and arousal
Regulation of appetite and feeding behavior
Modulation of energy homeostasis and metabolism
Involvement in reward and motivation pathways
Regulation of autonomic and neuroendocrine functions
Potential neuroprotective effects under investigation
peptides.dosageRange: Unknown
peptides.mechanism: Orexin B binds preferentially to the orexin-2 receptor (OX2R), a G-protein coupled receptor, with roughly equal affinity to orexin A at OX2R but significantly lower affinity at OX1R. Activation of OX2R triggers Gq-mediated intracellular calcium signaling, depolarization of target neurons, and downstream excitatory effects on arousal, feeding, and autonomic circuits.
contraindications: Individuals with cardiovascular instability (orexin signaling affects sympathetic tone)
Concurrent use of orexin receptor antagonists (pharmacological antagonism)
Pregnancy and lactation (insufficient safety data)
Known hypersensitivity to orexin peptides
sideEffects: Increased blood pressure and heart rate
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical, not approved for human therapeutic use. Orexin receptor agonists are under clinical investigation for narcolepsy treatment.

peptides.description: Oxytocin fragment most commonly refers to the C-terminal tripeptide Pro-Leu-Gly-NH2, also known as MIF-1 (Melanocyte-Inhibiting Factor 1) or PLG. peptides.name: Relaxin-2 (Human Relaxin H2)
peptides.description: Relaxin is a peptide hormone belonging to the insulin superfamily, primarily produced by the corpus luteum during pregnancy but also expressed in other tissues including the heart, brain, and kidneys. It is a two-chain (A and B chain) peptide of approximately 6 kDa that signals through the relaxin family peptide receptor 1 (RXFP1). Research has investigated its roles in connective tissue remodeling, cardiovascular function, fibrosis reduction, and vasodilation, with recombinant human relaxin-2 (serelaxin) having been studied in clinical trials for acute heart failure.

Anti-fibrotic effects investigated in cardiac, renal, and hepatic fibrosis

Renal hemodynamic effects including increased renal blood flow
Anti-inflammatory properties observed in preclinical models

It also inhibits TGF-β/Smad signaling, reducing collagen deposition and myofibroblast differentiation.

peptides.name: Secretin
peptides.description: Secretin is a 27-amino acid peptide hormone produced by S cells of the duodenum in response to acidic chyme entering the small intestine. It was the first hormone to be identified, discovered by Bayliss and Starling in 1902. Secretin primarily stimulates the pancreas to secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid and inhibits gastric acid secretion. Research has also investigated its roles in water homeostasis, biliary function, and as a diagnostic agent for pancreatic and gastrinoma evaluation.
benefits: Stimulates pancreatic bicarbonate secretion to neutralize duodenal acid
Inhibits gastric acid secretion
Stimulates bile flow from the liver (choleretic effect)
Used as a diagnostic aid for pancreatic exocrine function testing

peptides.mechanism: Secretin binds to secretin receptors (SCTR), a class B G protein-coupled receptor, on pancreatic ductal cells and other target tissues, activating adenylyl cyclase and increasing intracellular cAMP levels. This leads to activation of CFTR chloride channels and subsequent bicarbonate and water secretion from pancreatic duct cells, while also inhibiting gastrin release and gastric acid output.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to secretin
Acute pancreatitis (relative contraindication)
History of allergic reaction to porcine-derived secretin (for porcine preparations)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: FDA-approved as a diagnostic agent (synthetic human secretin marketed as ChiRhoStim and previously SecreFloTM) for stimulation of pancreatic secretions and for diagnosis of gastrinoma

peptides.name: Somatostatin (Somatotropin Release-Inhibiting Factor)
peptides.description: Somatostatin is a cyclic peptide hormone naturally produced in the hypothalamus, gastrointestinal tract, and pancreatic delta cells. It exists in two bioactive forms: SST-14 (14 amino acids) and SST-28 (28 amino acids). It functions as a potent inhibitor of growth hormone, insulin, glucagon, and numerous gastrointestinal hormones. Research has extensively investigated its role in regulating endocrine and exocrine secretion, and synthetic analogs (octreotide, lanreotide) are widely used in clinical medicine for neuroendocrine tumors and acromegaly.
benefits: Inhibition of growth hormone secretion
Suppression of insulin and glucagon release
Inhibition of gastrointestinal hormone secretion
Reduction of splanchnic blood flow
Antiproliferative effects on neuroendocrine tumor cells
Control of gastrointestinal bleeding
peptides.dosageRange: Native SST-14: 250 mcg bolus IV or 250-500 mcg/hr infusion (clinical settings); synthetic analogs used at different doses
peptides.frequency: Continuous IV infusion or repeated dosing due to very short half-life; synthetic analogs allow less frequent dosing
peptides.mechanism: Somatostatin binds to five G-protein-coupled receptor subtypes (SSTR1-5), activating inhibitory Gi/Go proteins. This leads to inhibition of adenylyl cyclase, reduction of intracellular cAMP, activation of potassium channels, and inhibition of voltage-dependent calcium channels, resulting in suppression of hormone secretion, reduction of cell proliferation, and modulation of neurotransmission.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to somatostatin or its analogs
Patients with poorly controlled diabetes (risk of severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia due to insulin/glucagon modulation)
Caution in patients with cardiac conduction abnormalities
Pregnancy and lactation (insufficient safety data)
commonStacks: Proton pump inhibitors (in GI bleeding protocols)
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Native somatostatin is used clinically in some countries for acute variceal bleeding and diagnostic testing. Synthetic analogs (octreotide, lanreotide, pasireotide) are FDA-approved for acromegaly and neuroendocrine tumors. Native somatostatin itself is not FDA-approved as a standalone drug in the United States.

peptides.name: Octreotide
peptides.description: Octreotide is a synthetic octapeptide analogue of somatostatin that inhibits growth hormone, glucagon, and insulin secretion. It is more potent and longer-acting than native somatostatin. It was developed by Sandoz (now Novartis) and has been extensively studied and approved for acromegaly, carcinoid tumors, and vasoactive intestinal peptide-secreting tumors (VIPomas). Research has also investigated its role in managing gastrointestinal bleeding, pancreatic fistulas, and various neuroendocrine conditions.
benefits: Suppression of excessive growth hormone secretion in acromegaly
Reduction of symptoms associated with carcinoid and VIP-secreting tumors
Control of acute variceal and gastrointestinal hemorrhage
Reduction of pancreatic and gastrointestinal fistula output
Inhibition of inappropriate insulin secretion in insulinomas
Management of diarrhea associated with neuroendocrine tumors
