peptides.frequency: 2-3x daily (subcutaneous immediate-release) or once monthly (long-acting release/LAR depot)
peptides.mechanism: Octreotide binds to somatostatin receptors (primarily SSTR2 and SSTR5) on target cells, inhibiting the secretion of growth hormone, insulin, glucagon, gastrin, and other gastrointestinal and pancreatic peptides. It also reduces splanchnic blood flow and inhibits gastrointestinal motility and secretion.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to octreotide or any component of the formulation
Caution in patients with diabetes mellitus due to altered glucose regulation
Caution in patients with gallbladder disease or history of cholelithiasis
Caution in patients with renal or hepatic impairment

peptides.regulatoryStatus: FDA-approved for treatment of acromegaly, severe diarrhea/flushing associated with metastatic carcinoid tumors, and profuse watery diarrhea associated with VIPomas. Marketed as Sandostatin and Sandostatin LAR Depot.

peptides.name: Lanreotide
peptides.description: Lanreotide is a synthetic octapeptide analogue of somatostatin that inhibits the secretion of growth hormone, insulin, and various gastrointestinal hormones. It is a cyclic peptide containing a disulfide bridge and a D-naphthylalanine residue. Lanreotide is FDA-approved for the treatment of acromegaly, gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs), and carcinoid syndrome. Research has investigated its antiproliferative effects on various tumor types and its role in controlling hormone hypersecretion.

Antiproliferative effects on gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
Reduction of symptoms associated with carcinoid syndrome

Potential stabilization of tumor growth in GEP-NETs

This binding suppresses growth hormone secretion from the pituitary, inhibits secretion of various gastrointestinal and pancreatic hormones, and exerts direct and indirect antiproliferative effects on neuroendocrine tumor cells.

Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus (may alter glucose homeostasis)
Severe hepatic impairment (dose adjustment may be required)
Known gallbladder disease or history of biliary complications
peptides.regulatoryStatus: FDA-approved for the long-term treatment of acromegaly, treatment of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs), and carcinoid syndrome. Marketed as Somatuline Depot (Ipsen).

peptides.name: Pasireotide (SOM230)
peptides.description: Pasireotide is a synthetic cyclohexapeptide somatostatin analogue that binds with high affinity to somatostatin receptor subtypes 1, 2, 3, and 5, with particularly strong affinity for subtype 5. It was developed by Novartis and is marketed under the brand name Signifor. Research and clinical use have focused on its ability to suppress ACTH and cortisol secretion in Cushing's disease, as well as its role in controlling growth hormone secretion in acromegaly.

peptides.name: Substance P

peptides.description: SS-20 is a synthetic mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide developed by Hazel Szeto and colleagues. peptides.name: Glucose-dependent Insulinotropic Peptide (Gastric Inhibitory Polypeptide)
peptides.description: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) is a 42-amino acid incretin hormone secreted by enteroendocrine K-cells of the duodenum and jejunum in response to nutrient ingestion. It stimulates insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells in a glucose-dependent manner and plays roles in lipid metabolism and bone remodeling. Research has investigated its role in type 2 diabetes, obesity, and metabolic regulation, and GIP receptor agonism is now a component of dual-incretin therapeutic strategies such as tirzepatide.

peptides.mechanism: GIP binds to the GIP receptor (GIPR), a G-protein coupled receptor expressed on pancreatic beta cells, adipocytes, osteoblasts, and neurons. Receptor activation increases intracellular cAMP via adenylyl cyclase, which in beta cells potentiates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion through PKA and Epac2 signaling pathways, and in adipocytes promotes lipid uptake and storage.

peptides.regulatoryStatus: Native GIP is an endogenous hormone not independently approved as a therapeutic. Standalone GIP analogs remain research compounds.

peptides.name: Maridebart cafraglutide (MariTide)
peptides.description: MariTide (maridebart cafraglutide) is a novel bispecific antibody-peptide conjugate developed by Amgen for the treatment of obesity. It combines an anti-GIP receptor antagonist antibody (maridebart) conjugated to a GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide (cafraglutide), creating a dual-action molecule. Research is investigating its potential for significant body weight reduction with less frequent dosing (monthly or less) compared to existing GLP-1 receptor agonists. It is currently in Phase 2/3 clinical trials.

This bispecific approach simultaneously blocks GIP signaling and activates GLP-1 signaling, resulting in reduced appetite and caloric intake, with the antibody scaffold providing an extended half-life enabling infrequent dosing.

peptides.name: Danuglipron

Research has investigated its effects on glycemic control, body weight reduction, and metabolic parameters in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity.

By activating GLP-1R, it enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon release, slows gastric emptying, and reduces appetite via central nervous system signaling.

peptides.name: Angiotensin-(1-7)

It acts as a counter-regulatory peptide to angiotensin II, opposing its vasoconstrictive, pro-inflammatory, and pro-fibrotic effects. Research has investigated its roles in cardiovascular protection, metabolic regulation, anti-inflammatory signaling, and organ protection in models of heart failure, diabetes, and lung injury.

peptides.name: Apelin-13 ([Pyr1]apelin-13)

Research has investigated apelin-13's roles in cardiovascular function, glucose metabolism, fluid homeostasis, and angiogenesis. The pyroglutaminated form ([Pyr1]apelin-13) is the predominant circulating isoform and is more resistant to enzymatic degradation.

peptides.name: Irisin (FNDC5 cleavage product)
peptides.description: Irisin is a myokine hormone cleaved from the transmembrane protein FNDC5 (fibronectin type III domain-containing protein 5), primarily released by skeletal muscle during exercise. It was first identified in 2012 by Boström et al. and has been investigated for its role in browning of white adipose tissue, thermogenesis, and energy metabolism. Research has also explored its potential roles in bone metabolism, neuroprotection, and glucose homeostasis.

It also signals through integrin αVβ5 receptors on osteocytes and adipocytes to regulate bone remodeling and energy metabolism.

Research has investigated its roles in appetite regulation, lipid metabolism, glucose homeostasis, and body weight control. Circulating spexin levels have been found to be reduced in obese individuals and those with type 2 diabetes, suggesting a role in metabolic regulation.

peptides.name: Asprosin
peptides.description: Asprosin is a fasting-induced glucogenic protein hormone discovered in 2016. It is a 140-amino acid C-terminal cleavage product of profibrillin (encoded by FBN1). Asprosin is primarily secreted by white adipose tissue and acts on the liver to promote hepatic glucose release via the OR4M1 receptor and cAMP-PKA pathway. Research has investigated its roles in glucose homeostasis, appetite regulation via hypothalamic AgRP neurons, insulin resistance, and metabolic disorders including type 2 diabetes and obesity.

It also crosses the blood-brain barrier and activates hypothalamic AgRP+ neurons to stimulate appetite while inhibiting POMC+ neurons, linking it to both peripheral glucose regulation and central appetite control.

peptides.name: Fibroblast Growth Factor 21
peptides.description: Fibroblast Growth Factor 21 (FGF-21) is a 181-amino acid endocrine hormone primarily produced by the liver in response to metabolic stress, fasting, and certain dietary conditions. It acts as a key regulator of energy homeostasis, glucose and lipid metabolism, and insulin sensitivity. Research has investigated FGF-21 and its analogs for their potential roles in treating obesity, type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), and cardiovascular disease. Several engineered FGF-21 analogs (e.g., pegbelfermin, efruxifermin) have been developed to improve pharmacokinetic properties and are undergoing clinical trials.
benefits: Improved insulin sensitivity and glucose homeostasis
Enhanced fatty acid oxidation and lipid metabolism
Reduction in hepatic steatosis and liver fat
Body weight reduction in preclinical and clinical studies
Improvement in dyslipidemia markers including triglycerides
Potential cardioprotective effects
peptides.dosageRange: Varies by analog; native FGF-21 research doses vary widely; clinical analogs (e.g., pegbelfermin) studied at 10-20 mg weekly
peptides.frequency: Once weekly to once daily depending on analog and formulation
peptides.halfLife: Native FGF-21: ~1-2 hours; engineered analogs: 3-5 days
peptides.mechanism: FGF-21 signals through FGF receptor 1c (FGFR1c) in complex with the co-receptor beta-Klotho (KLB), activating downstream pathways including ERK1/2 and Akt signaling in metabolic tissues such as adipose tissue, liver, and pancreas. This leads to enhanced glucose uptake, increased fatty acid oxidation, improved mitochondrial function, and modulation of energy expenditure and thermogenesis.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to FGF-21 or its analogs
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (insufficient safety data)
Severe hepatic impairment (requires further study)
Bone health concerns (preclinical data suggest potential effects on bone metabolism)
sideEffects: Potential effects on bone mineral density (preclinical concern)
Elevated heart rate observed in some studies
peptides.regulatoryStatus: Research chemical and investigational drug. Native FGF-21 is not approved for therapeutic use. Several FGF-21 analogs (pegbelfermin, efruxifermin) are in Phase 2/3 clinical trials for NASH, obesity, and metabolic disorders but are not yet FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Klotho (α-Klotho protein)
peptides.description: Klotho is a transmembrane protein originally discovered in 1997 that also exists as a soluble circulating factor. It is primarily expressed in the kidneys, brain, and parathyroid glands. Soluble α-Klotho functions as a humoral factor involved in mineral metabolism, oxidative stress resistance, and aging suppression. Research has investigated its role in longevity, cognitive enhancement, kidney protection, and age-related disease modulation, as mice deficient in Klotho exhibit accelerated aging phenotypes while overexpression extends lifespan.

peptides.halfLife: Unknown — soluble Klotho clearance in humans has not been precisely characterized for therapeutic use
peptides.mechanism: Soluble α-Klotho acts as a co-receptor for fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) to regulate phosphate homeostasis and vitamin D metabolism. It also independently suppresses Wnt signaling, inhibits insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathways, enhances FGF signaling, reduces oxidative stress by upregulating manganese superoxide dismutase, and modulates ion channel activity at the cell surface, collectively contributing to its anti-aging effects.
contraindications: No established human contraindications due to limited clinical use

Caution warranted in individuals with hypophosphatemia
sideEffects: No well-documented human side effect profile due to preclinical stage of research

peptides.name: Sirtuin Activating Peptides
peptides.description: Sirtuin activating peptides are a class of short peptide sequences designed to activate sirtuin family deacetylases (SIRT1-SIRT7), which are NAD+-dependent enzymes involved in cellular stress responses, metabolism, and aging. These peptides are investigated in preclinical research for their potential roles in modulating longevity-associated pathways, mitochondrial function, and epigenetic regulation. They represent an emerging area of research distinct from small-molecule sirtuin activators like resveratrol, leveraging peptide-based approaches to achieve targeted sirtuin modulation.

This activation promotes downstream effects including PGC-1α-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis, FOXO transcription factor activation, and suppression of NF-κB-driven inflammatory pathways.
